newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: Bolivia March annualized inflation at 30-year low.
newsitem.headline: Bolivia March annualized inflation at 30-year low.

text.p: Bolivian annualized inflation in March dropped to its lowest level in three decades at 3.62 percent, after month-on-month consumer price deflation of 0.24 percent, the government said Wednesday.

Bolivia has now registered monthly falls in the consumer price index twice this year, taking the accumulated inflation rate for the first quarter to minus 0.06 percent, said the National Statistics Institute's director Juan Brun.
He said inflation was a monthly 0.19 percent in February because of transport problems caused by heavy rain, but this was compensated the next month by a boom in farm production.

The latest March figure compares with 0.22 percent deflation the same month last year, but accumulated inflation for the first quarter of that year was much higher at 4.12 percent, and annualized inflation last March was 14.54 percent.
The Bolivian government forecasts 1997 annual inflation of a maximum 7.5 percent, versus 7.95 percent for 1996.
